messages:
Kate L: Starting blue->green traffic siphon for release v2.3. Change window 02:00-03:00 UTC. Plan: 0% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 20m steps. Pre-warm caches and pin sessions to new backend during shift. @oncall-bot please watch p95 and 5xx.

Sam T: got it. prep checklist posted: RN-487 link: https://intranet.redwood/release/RN-487 :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy run triggered by Sam T at 02:05 UTC
deploy-bot: action=route-update target=green percent=10 rollout_phase=step1

Morgan: Observability note — enabling slow-path tracing for green during warmup.

infra-bot: metric snapshot @02:08 UTC - green p50=120ms p95=430ms 5xx=0.2% traffic=10%

Sam T: increase to 30% after 5m if 5xx < 1% and p95 stable. proceeding in 5.

deploy-bot: action=route-update target=green percent=30 rollout_phase=step2

infra-bot: metric snapshot @02:15 UTC - green p50=130ms p95=490ms 5xx=1.8% traffic=30% :eyes:

Ryan: seeing slight spike on reload endpoint, spike concentrated on /internal/cache/refresh - throttling at app layer.

Kate L: hold for 3m. @Morgan pull logs for that endpoint and - if error rate >2% revert to 10% and notify.

Morgan: pulled logs, confirmed burst caused by parallel refreshes from worker pool. I pushed a hotfix to throttle refreshes; patch id: pr/6126

Sam T: re-run canary step in 3.

deploy-bot: action=route-update target=green percent=30 rollout_phase=reapply

infra-bot: metric snapshot @02:26 UTC - green p50=125ms p95=420ms 5xx=0.4% traffic=30%

Kate L: good. moving to 60% in next step.

deploy-bot: action=route-update target=green percent=60 rollout_phase=step3

infra-bot: metric snapshot @02:34 UTC - green p50=128ms p95=435ms 5xx=0.3% traffic=60%

Sam T: final 100% after 10m if stable. session pinning set: cookie=rdw_sid backend=green

deploy-bot: action=route-update target=green percent=100 rollout_phase=complete timestamp=02:45 UTC

oncall-bot: change window closed. All systems nominal. :tada:

Kate L: release notes RN-487 updated with post-deploy artifacts and rollback tag 'rollback-3605002468' in case. Thanks team.
